dedupe_keys.name: deep de risking energy efficiency platform energy efficiency project performance database

description: DEEP, the European Commission's De-risking Energy Efficiency Platform, is an open-source database for monitoring and benchmarking the performance of energy efficiency investments in buildings and industry, aiming to raise efficiency financing through market evidence on real risks and benefits. After a July 2026 update that added 52,900 projects from Germany and the United States, it covers more than 89,400 projects; the home page listed 54,191 building projects without on-site renewables, with a median payback of 3.9 years and a median avoidance cost of 2.9 euro cents per kWh, and 28,893 industry projects. Further European data from EIB/ELENA and national agencies were expected later in 2026. Coverage: mainly European projects, now with U.S. data. Access: charts are public; registered users see anonymised historical data by project characteristics and can upload private projects to benchmark against chosen subsets. Licence: platform terms. Caveats: records are anonymised and aggregated, and the sources differ by provider and period. Simulation uses: realistic cost, savings and payback distributions for retrofit investment models. Related records: the EU Building Stock Observatory and the Hotmaps building stock maps. Note: the recall candidate's address deep.eu belongs to an unrelated company.
